proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is the right (power) to alienate, consume, or destroy a thing — one of the three classical sticks in the Roman dominium bundle (usus, fructus, abusus). In BFO terms it is a Role: it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a legal person (the owner), is externally grounded in the legal system's recognition of ownership, and is realised in acts of alienation or consumption. It is a subtype of LegalRight (already a Role subclass in the working ontology), capturing the specific right-dimension concerned with disposition-over-substance rather than use or fruits.

entities.label: RightOfAlienation
entities.rationale: One canonical exercise of abusus is the power to transfer title (alienation). Modelling this as a subclass of Abusus allows fine-grained typing of specific incidents of the broader abuse-right.

entities.label: ActOfAlienation
entities.rationale: Abusus (as a realizable Role) is realised in processes of alienation, consumption, or destruction. ActOfAlienation captures the occurrent in which the role is exercised, needed for the BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of legal right, inheriting the Role typing already established for LegalRight in the working ontology.
RightOfAlienation is one specific incident falling under the broader abusus dimension of ownership.
The abusus role is realised in (BFO_0000054) acts of alienation or consumption — occurrents of class ActOfAlienation.

open_questions: Should Abusus be typed as a class (representing the kind 'right of abuse' in general) or also instantiated as an individual representing the specific Roman-law doctrine? Currently modelled as a class.

Roman dominium also includes Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits). Should these sibling classes be minted now to complete the bundle, with a parent class OwnershipRight or DominiumIncident?
Should ActOfAlienation be further specialised to cover consumption/destruction (consumptio, destructio) as distinct subclasses, or is one process class sufficient for this analysis?
Should a DominiumRole class be introduced as the common parent of Usus, Fructus, and Abusus under LegalRight, to represent the Roman law bundle of ownership incidents?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the Roman-law dimension of dominium conferring on the owner the power to alienate, consume, or destroy the res. In BFO 2020 it is best captured as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a legal person qua owner, is externally grounded by the legal system's recognition criteria (not internally grounded like a disposition), and is realised in concrete processes of alienation or destruction. It is typed as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight, which is already a Role subclass. A companion process class ActOfAlienation (BFO_0000015) is introduced to serve as the realisation target via BFO_0000054. A subclass RightOfAlienation is also proposed to distinguish the transfer-of-title incident from consumption/destruction incidents, preserving granularity for downstream legal reasoning.
